description:
I have identified a River Birch (Betula nigra) at 2:57 PM on October 18th. What makes this tree very identifiable is the bark. The bark is a reddish-brown color that looks like pealing paper and gives it a rugged appearance. The leaves are simple, alternate with a doubly serrated margin. The leaves are bigger at the bottom and becomes smaller as it gets to the top of the leaf. I would say the leaf shape is oblique. They can grow to be 40-70 feet tall.

When this tree was identified it was 58 degrees with a high of 63 degrees and a low of 41 degrees for the day. With a wind speed of about 4 mph. Overall it was a cloudy and chilly day. 

I found this River Birch growing alongside another River Birch (Betula nigra) and some smaller shrubs that I was unable to identify. They typically grow best in moist, well-drained soils in full to partial sun exposure. They can often be found with Sweetgum (Liquidambar styraciflua) and Sycamore (Platanus occidentalis) trees along a stream bank.
